Definition: from G1520 repeated with G2596 inserted; severally:--one by one.
BiblicalUsage: Heis kath' heis means one by one, each in turn, and it appears once, at the table on the night of the betrayal. In Mark 14:19 the disciples begin every one to say to Jesus, is it I, one by one, each asking in turn whether he is the traitor.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the phrase is the saddest in the supper: not one of them points at another, each one asks about himself, and each one is right to be afraid.
